title: Treatment Decision Points: When to Continue, Change, or Reassess
summary: Clinical decision framework for interpreting disease monitoring results and determining whether to continue current treatment, escalate, modify, or switch to alternative approaches.

content.text: Treatment Decisions Based on Disease Monitoring

Interpretation of disease monitoring data drives critical treatment decisions. This framework outlines common clinical scenarios and general principles for deciding whether to continue, modify, or change treatment.
All target lesions resolved, no new lesions, non-target disease stable or resolved.

items: Confirm CR is maintained on repeat imaging (not a transient finding)
Assess timing: CR after 2 cycles vs after full planned course have different implications
Consider consolidation therapy if applicable (e.g., radiation to residual mass site)
Continue current therapy per planned protocol if early CR (maintain benefit)
Complete planned course then stop if final CR achieved (avoid unnecessary toxicity)
Consider maintenance therapy if high-risk disease (e.g., aggressive histology, advanced stage)
Transition to surveillance with periodic imaging and clinic visits

content.text: ≥30% decrease in target lesion sum, no new lesions.

items: Indicates drug efficacy; tumor is responding to treatment
Continue current therapy to maximize response (may achieve CR with additional cycles)
Assess toxicity: If severe, dose modifications may be needed
Some patients convert from PR to CR with additional treatment cycles (20-40% of cases)
Continue current therapy: Complete planned course
Assess tolerance: Reduce dose or extend intervals if significant toxicity
Re-image at next planned interval to assess for further response
Do not change therapy unless: new or worsening toxicity, patient request, or development of contraindication

content.text: Stable Disease (SD): Neither Shrinkage nor Growth
<30% decrease and <20% increase in target lesion sum, no new lesions.

items: Indicates disease not progressing; some therapeutic benefit (halted growth)
Benefit varies by cancer type: SD may be favorable in slow-growing tumors, less favorable in aggressive types
May indicate inadequate dosing, inadequate drug exposure, or partial drug resistance
Duration of SD matters: 6+ months SD may warrant continuation; early SD (≤3 months) may suggest inadequate response
Continue current therapy if: well tolerated, early in planned course, SD maintained >3-6 months
Change therapy if: SD present <3 months, biomarkers indicate progression, or patient has clinical decline
Dose escalation: Consider if initial doses conservative (check if patient at full therapeutic dose)
Re-image sooner (4-6 weeks) if concerned about early progression; otherwise standard interval

content.text: ≥20% increase in target lesion sum OR new lesions OR worsening non-target disease.

items: Current therapy not effective; continuation likely futile
Requires prompt reassessment to confirm diagnosis and assess pace of progression
Assess for treatable complications: infection, VTE, cardiac complications that may mimic progression
Discuss with patient: may prompt discussion of clinical trial eligibility, palliative care integration
Confirm PD: Repeat imaging within 1-2 weeks to ensure not technical artifact
Change therapy: Consider next-line regimen based on disease type and prior treatments
Molecular profiling: If not done, consider tumor sequencing to identify resistance mechanism
Dose reduction not recommended: PD reflects inadequate efficacy, not excess toxicity
Consider clinical trials: If available for this disease type and stage
Declining ECOG score may warrant stopping treatment despite SD/PR (consider quality of life)
Improvement in performance status with treatment continuation generally indicates continued benefit
New comorbidities or organ dysfunction may necessitate drug changes (not due to disease but due to tolerability)
Tumor markers (CEA, PSA, CA-125) often correlate with imaging response but may lag behind
Rising markers with stable imaging warrants re-imaging sooner to detect early progression
Falling markers with stable imaging suggests benefit; continue therapy
Markers can normalize before imaging resolution (anticipated in good responders)
Clinical deterioration despite imaging SD warrants investigation (complications vs occult progression)
Symptom improvement with imaging PR indicates good response; continue therapy
New symptoms with imaging progression suggests urgent change or escalation needed
Quality of life decline may warrant stopping treatment even with imaging response (patient-centered decision)
Grade 3-4 toxicity with poor response (SD/PD): Stop or significantly modify therapy
Grade 3-4 toxicity with good response (PR/CR): May continue with dose reduction if necessary
Cumulative toxicity (e.g., cardiac, renal): May necessitate stopping therapy despite response
Reversible vs irreversible toxicity: Plan differently (reversible may improve with break; irreversible warrants stopping)

content.text: Appropriate when: CR or PR achieved, well tolerated, per protocol plan, early in course.
Appropriate when: Response adequate (PR/CR) but significant toxicity, patient tolerating poorly, cumulative organ toxicity risk. Disadvantage: May reduce efficacy.
Appropriate when: Residual disease after systemic therapy (add radiation), inadequate response (consider adding second drug), or early progression (add targeted agent if available).
Appropriate when: PD on current therapy, acquired resistance suspected, or next-line standard regimen indicated. Should be based on disease type, molecular findings, and available options.
Appropriate when: CR achieved (planned end), intolerable toxicity, patient decline, poor prognosis with no better options, or patient preference for palliative approach.

items: Tumor board review recommended for: Unusual responses, treatment-resistant disease, major therapy changes
Discuss with patient/family: All major decisions (therapy change, stopping treatment, clinical trial entry)
Coordination with palliative care: Important for PD patients, declining performance status, or limited prognosis
Molecular tumor boards: If genetic testing identifies actionable mutations, consider targeted therapy options

rows: Confirm CR persists; consider maintenance if high-risk
Assess tolerance; may achieve CR with more cycles
Continue if tolerated and >3 months SD; otherwise change
Per protocol or sooner if concern
Duration matters: early SD (<3mo) may warrant change
Change therapy or stop; confirm diagnosis
Confirm PD; assess cause; consider molecular profiling
